settings.heading: Discipline. Excellence. Mastery.
settings.subheading: Heirloom goods for an elite order devoted to virtue — forged from the beauty of Rome and dedicated to the glory of God.

settings.title: Courage
settings.text: To act rightly in the face of fear.

settings.title: Wisdom
settings.text: To see clearly and choose well.

settings.title: Temperance
settings.text: To master oneself before all else.

settings.heading: Made to be kept
settings.text: Nothing mass-produced. Everything carved, cast, woven, or bound to last.

settings.heading: The discipline of the inner citadel
settings.text: Long before our order, the Stoics taught that virtue is the only good — and that a life of discipline, resilience, and self-mastery is freedom. We build in that same spirit.

settings.name: Marcus Aurelius
settings.quote: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.

settings.name: Seneca
settings.quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.

settings.name: Epictetus
settings.quote: It is not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.

settings.name: Cato the Younger
settings.quote: Esse quam videri — to be, rather than to seem.

settings.heading: Studied, not worshipped
settings.text: Figures of history — remembered for leadership, courage, and excellence, and for the hard lessons their lives still teach. Sources of inspiration, held with nuance.

settings.name: Marcus Aurelius
settings.summary: The philosopher-emperor who governed through war and plague, and left the Meditations — a private record of duty, restraint, and Stoic resolve.

settings.name: Scipio Africanus
settings.summary: The commander who ended the Second Punic War at Zama. Remembered for strategy and clemency — and for withdrawing from public life rather than clinging to power.

settings.name: Leonidas I
settings.summary: Led the stand at Thermopylae against overwhelming odds. A lasting symbol of duty and sacrifice in service of others.

settings.name: Julius Caesar
settings.summary: General, reformer, and author whose ambition reshaped Rome — and ended its Republic. A study in brilliance and its costs.

settings.name: Alexander the Great
settings.summary: Carried Greek culture across three continents by his early thirties. His empire fragmented at his death — a lesson in the limits of conquest.

settings.heading: Guardians in marble and bronze
settings.text: Michael the defender, Gabriel the messenger, Raphael the healer — carved as sculpture, and rendered in three dimensions.

settings.name: Saint Michael
settings.text: Quis ut Deus? — captain of the host of Heaven.

settings.name: Saint Gabriel
settings.text: Who carried the word that changed the world.

settings.name: Saint Raphael
settings.text: God heals — companion of the traveler.

settings.heading: Trusted by an order that endures
What endures
settings.text: Christ is King. His is the kingdom that outlasts every empire. We tell the old story of light and shadow to remember what endures — and to make things worthy of it.

settings.heading: The Kingdom that endures
settings.text: Earthly empires rise and fall, but the Kingdom of Christ endures forever.
